facts: Public PCS reset is synchronized into pmareset, which drives both TX and RX startup FSM SOFT_RESET.
While SOFT_RESET is 1, RX FSM stays INIT with GTRXRESET=0; TX stays INIT with GTTXRESET=0. Public reset held does not imply GT reset pins held high.
After SOFT_RESET releases, native approximately500ns startup wait runs, then ASSERT_ALL_RESETS drives GTRXRESET/GTTXRESET high. Native500ns logic is unchanged.
Original PCS public reset follows global268435455-cycle SYS POR, nominal2.14748364seconds at125MHz.
F403 public PCS reset follows not SYS_LOCKED. Existing synchronization and native startup wait remain; global SiTCP POR is unchanged.
hypothesis: Shorten the interval before the first actual GT reset sequence instead of adding another reset later. This may prevent an unfavorable RX/PMA-CDR startup state formed while the native FSM is held in INIT with GTRXRESET low.
limits: Source-derived ordering, not a measured power-on GT waveform.
Does not identify the rail, reference-clock behavior, analog component, or board variation initiating failure.
A successful independent F403 source trial is required; F402 early diagnostic alone retains unused timer.
